## Summary

- Capture the PR head before review lanes run in `agent-review.yml`.
- Add reviewed-head synthesis marker helpers and stamp review comments only when the PR head still matches.
- Add focused tests for stable head stamping, changed head omission, and marker parsing.
- Document reviewed-head provenance in supported workflows.

## Verification

- `npm run build`
- `node --test dist/__tests__/review-synthesis.test.js dist/__tests__/response.test.js dist/__tests__/post-comment-cli.test.js`
- YAML parse check for `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml`
- `git diff --check`

Closes #171

## AI Review Synthesis

<!-- sepo-agent-review-synthesis -->

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.
> Requested by @lolipopshock.

## Summary of PR/Issue
- PR #172 implements the first review-provenance slice from parent issue #170 via child issue #171.
- The PR captures the PR head before review lanes run, stamps synthesis comments with a reviewed-head marker only when the head is unchanged, adds marker parsing helpers, and updates focused tests/docs.
- This provenance is intended to support later self-approval trust checks without adding the self-approval route, orchestrator transitions, approval submission, or status-upsert polish in this slice.
- The design is directionally aligned with the split plan, but the current branch leaves the review workflow tests failing and introduces a hard workflow gate around best-effort metadata capture.

## Review
The core implementation is well-scoped, but it is not merge-ready. Two blocking issues need a branch update before this PR can ship.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Envelope tests still fail against the new review DAG | BLOCKING | `.agent` `npm test` fails with 499 passing and 2 failing tests because [`envelope.test.ts`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fddd0d7bc65e0fcb281701facd6523cec8d50e50/.agent/src/__tests__/envelope.test.ts#L364) still asserts the old `agent-review.yml` shape. |
| Head capture now hard-gates review output | BLOCKING | [`prepare`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fddd0d7bc65e0fcb281701facd6523cec8d50e50/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L82) now gates review jobs, so a metadata capture failure can skip all review output instead of degrading to a no-marker synthesis. |
| `rubrics-review` is serialized behind unused prepare output | WARNING | [`rubrics-review`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/fddd0d7bc65e0fcb281701facd6523cec8d50e50/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L227) depends on `prepare` but does not consume `reviewed_head_sha`, adding coupling and latency without a clear data dependency. |

## Progress
- Rubrics review passed and confirmed the PR matches the #170/#171 split, reuses typed helpers, and updates docs.
- Existing PR discussion already noted the `rubrics-review` dependency as INFO; I did not duplicate that as an inline comment.
- Posted inline comments on [`agent-review.yml#L82`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/172#discussion_r3211828318) and [`agent-review.yml#L121`](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/172#discussion_r3211828320).
- No existing inline comments were minimized or replied to.

## Issue Details
<details>
<summary>Envelope tests still fail against the new review DAG</summary>

**Cause:** The workflow now inserts `prepare`, changes `review` to `needs: [prepare]`, and changes `synthesize` to `needs: [prepare, review]`, but the envelope contract tests still expect the old layout.

**Candidate solutions:** Update the envelope tests to assert the new `prepare` job, the new `needs` graph, and the `REVIEWED_HEAD_SHA` handoff into `post-comment`.

**Comments:** I reproduced the failure with `.agent` `npm test`; GitHub currently reports the `check` job failing too.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Head capture now hard-gates review output</summary>

**Cause:** `prepare` is required by downstream review jobs, but `capture-pr-head.js` throws on missing PR metadata or failed lookup. That turns best-effort provenance capture into a workflow-wide gate.

**Candidate solutions:** Make head capture degrade to an empty `reviewed_head_sha` while allowing review to continue, for example via a non-blocking capture step/job or a CLI fallback that sets no output marker on recoverable metadata failures.

**Comments:** This matters because #171 says default behavior outside provenance marker infrastructure should stay unchanged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`rubrics-review` is serialized behind unused prepare output</summary>

**Cause:** `rubrics-review` has `needs: [prepare]`, but it never reads `needs.prepare.outputs.reviewed_head_sha`.

**Candidate solutions:** Remove that dependency unless there is an intentional ordering reason; if there is, document it in the workflow or tests.

**Comments:** Reviewers disagreed on severity here: one marked it WARNING, while the rubrics review treated it as INFO. It is secondary to the blocking failures.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step
FIX_PR: the failing tests and review-gating regression are concrete branch changes and are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict
NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items
- [ ] Update the review workflow envelope tests to cover `prepare`, the new `needs` graph, and `REVIEWED_HEAD_SHA`.
- [ ] Make reviewed-head capture non-blocking so review still runs without a provenance marker when capture fails.

@sepo-agent /answer can you remind again why this is pr needed for implementing the agent self approval pr?

This PR is needed because agent self-approval needs a trusted answer to: **“was this exact PR head already reviewed and given SHIP?”**

PR #172 is the provenance slice. It does not implement self-approval itself; it adds the marker that later self-approval code can trust:

- `agent-review.yml` captures the PR head before reviewer lanes run and passes it into synthesis: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/adbb1dc7680384ed98e709c9f4ca201f1ec9bf89/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L82-L117 and https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/adbb1dc7680384ed98e709c9f4ca201f1ec9bf89/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L244-L358
- `post-comment.ts` only stamps the synthesis comment if the PR head still matches the captured head before posting: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/adbb1dc7680384ed98e709c9f4ca201f1ec9bf89/.agent/src/cli/post-comment.ts#L48-L69
- `review-synthesis.ts` adds the hidden reviewed-head marker and parser: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/adbb1dc7680384ed98e709c9f4ca201f1ec9bf89/.agent/src/review-synthesis.ts#L18-L25

The self-approval PR then builds on that. In PR #180, the resolver checks the latest trusted Sepo review synthesis, extracts the reviewed head marker, requires `SHIP`, and rejects approval if that reviewed head is not the current PR head: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b8d27c53f9e0610ebba395382909aa6cce15f431/.agent/src/self-approval.ts#L83-L158

So the safety chain is:

`review synthesis says SHIP for head H` -> `self-approval agent inspects head H` -> `deterministic resolver approves only if the PR is still at head H`.

Without PR #172, self-approval would only know “some review said SHIP”, not whether that SHIP applies to the exact commit being approved. That is the trust boundary this PR creates.

@sepo-agent /answer 

if our goal is ultimately to have agents self merge PRs, does it matter to track the review head SHAs?

Yes. For self-merge, tracking reviewed head SHAs matters even more.

The core safety rule should be:

`reviewed head == approved head == current head at merge time`

Without that, an agent could:

- review commit `A`
- PR changes to commit `B`
- self-approve or merge `B` using an old `SHIP` review from `A`

For self-approval, the reviewed-head marker proves “SHIP applied to this exact commit.” For self-merge, the merge resolver should do the same kind of deterministic recheck immediately before merging:

1. latest trusted review synthesis is `SHIP`
2. synthesis has reviewed-head SHA `H`
3. any self-approval, if required, inspected/approved SHA `H`
4. current PR head is still `H`
5. only then submit approval or merge

So the reviewed-head SHA is not just bookkeeping. It is the provenance anchor that prevents stale-review approval/merge races. It is not sufficient by itself, but it is one of the required inputs for safe self-merge.
